why: The registry entries, keys, budgets and the cron_due() row are written out, but the step carries two migrations (one a custom copy of commerce.cron_due() whose whole body must be taken from whichever of steps 3.1, 3.2 or 3.7 replaced it last) and rewires the daily jobs that hold the GDPR retention run, erasures and domain renewal invoicing, now retried up to three times a day. harm_if_wrong: A cron_due() copied from an older migration silently drops another step's job from the tick, or a daily job runs out of order or more often than intended (retention before erasures reversed, renewals retried), with the scans and int cases still green.
make_it_cheaper: Write the full DAILY_JOBS literal (every key, work kind, cap and budget for all 40 calls) into the brief and name the migration file whose cron_due() body is to be copied, so only the generated diff needs a glance.
brief_problems: Commit 1 makes pruneVisits() throw, but until commit 2 lands it still runs inside the route's first Promise.all at line 61, where a throw rejects the whole group and the rest of the daily route; commit 1 must not be pushed alone, and the brief does not say so.

commerce.cron_due(), runRegistry() and RegistryJob do not exist yet (steps 3.1 and 3.3); the custom migration must copy a body that later steps (3.2, 3.7) may also have replaced, and the brief does not name which file is newest.
